title: Existence of canonical spectrum chain coordinates
statement: For a cartesian affine scheme square and its cartesian global-section spectrum square [def-pc-scheme], a point z0 of Spec Γ(X', top), and a cochain complex P of modules on X, put z=X'.isoSpec.inv(z0), P0=(X.isoSpec.inv)*P, Q=P at g'(z), and Q0=P0 at g0'(z0) [def-pc-single-complex-base-change-stalk-condition]. Fix eA and eD to the actual canonicalSpectrumStalkEquiv maps of X.isoSpec.inv and X'.isoSpec.inv, including the point transport from isoSpec naturality [lem-pc-affine-spectrum-canonical-stalk-ring-coordinates]. There exists a chain isomorphism q:Q≅Res_eA(Q0). This component only asserts existence of q; the generator formula for a fixed q is a separate strict sub-obligation.

proof.text: For an isomorphism j, its stalk ring map rho is invertible. Restriction of scalars along rho is an equivalence; the extension/restriction adjunction unit is therefore invertible. Compose that unit with the inverse tensor-pullback stalk comparison, restricted along rho, obtaining an isomorphism of functors from the original stalk to the restricted pulled-back stalk.

Use additivity of tensor pullback and the module stalk functor to map the natural isomorphism to complexes; separate the composed functors with mapHomologicalComplexCompIso. Specialize to X.isoSpec.inv and transport the point by isoSpec_inv_naturality. Unfold canonicalSpectrumStalkEquiv to identify the fixed scalar map. The existential remainder is True.
